title: Power Update After K-th Largest Insertion II
summary: Given an integer array nums and an integer p, for each query insert a value into nums, find the k-th largest element, update p to p raised to the power of that element modulo 10^9 + 7, and return the final value of p after all queries.
statement: Given an integer array nums and an integer p, for each query insert a value into nums, find the k-th largest element, update p to p raised to the power of that element modulo 10^9 + 7, and return the final value of p after all queries.
constraints: nums and queries are nonempty; all values and p are positive and at most 10^9.
Each query [value,k] inserts value before selecting the kth largest current element.
Apply every modular exponentiation to the p produced by the preceding query.
hints: All inserted values are known before processing begins, so coordinate compression preserves their order.
A Fenwick tree stores the frequency of every compressed value.
After insertion, the kth largest is the element of ascending order size-k+1.
Fenwick binary lifting finds that order statistic in logarithmic time; modular exponentiation then updates the running value.
editorial: Fenwick binary lifting finds that order statistic in logarithmic time; modular exponentiation then updates the running value.

tests.explanation: After inserting three, the largest exponent is three; after inserting one, the second largest is two.
The selected exponents are four and seven, producing 1296 and then 220296870.
